scope: 19 normal specials. Rainmaker separately inspected but not part of this API.

guideContract.points: Vector3[], no game state writes; optional reusable pool
guideContract.complete: Static modeled terminal is determined; not a claim that future actors/terrain will stay unchanged
guideContract.targetDependent: Current target or defense snapshot only; no guaranteed endpoint ring
guideContract.activeOnly: Resolve actual active state and return null while no aim action exists
guideContract.time: Flight until contact. Explosion entries include post-contact startup independently.
guideContract.readinessApi: s3CanPredictSpecialTrajectory(actor): same actual-state gates as activeOnly; cheap enough to query every rendered frame
guideContract.presentationOwner: superChump returns special-vfx; existing target disc and twelve reticles retain sole ownership
guideContract.timeOrigin: Times start at the current release/launch snapshot, excluding future input/windup. Terrain/cooler native blast queue adds one 60 Hz tick; Booyah growth startup adds 40 ticks. First nonzero growth/damage is a later source frame.

clockEvidence: New tests feed 30/60/120 render intervals into actual FixedClock; native simulation remains 60 Hz. Directly calling raw Trizooka/InkVac update at arbitrary coarse dt is not the production scheduling contract. No additional integrator carry was retained.
confirmedChanges: Special launch geometry and force/position integrations shared with read-only preview.
Booyah contact/lifetime damage center no longer ground-snaps to an unrelated lower storey; paint keeps separate surface projection.
Cooler source stepping and placement use the same side-effect-free flight record and contact function.
Predictive contact queries use private collider copies and do not consume hit callbacks, damage, paint, ink, gauge, network events, or RNG.

Inkjet, Booyah and Stamp retain the baseline cloned launch-origin ownership after shared geometry extraction. This avoids retaining the reusable rt.v0 scratch reference; it does not change numeric launch tuning or the calculated origin. The final source18 and all-specials85 gates passed this version.

validation.newSpecialTrajectory: Final-source 18 / 18 named cases passed (positive 8+10 split, 768 MiB heap). Both groups used all-specials SHA 0006c33b3f88b11eb646b89fd2c49c24f89d103c1f20ea908a1f59b7287a3231, with source/test hashes recorded before and after and confirmed unchanged. Includes readiness API, VFX owner and deferred explosion timing assertions.
validation.existingAllSpecials: 85 / 85 named cases passed: 53 all-specials registrations and 32 imported kraken-dash-occlusion cases. Executed sequentially as 17 positive exact-name groups of 5 with a 768 MiB heap cap. Every group exited 0 with pass 5, fail 0, skipped 0 and exact registered-name coverage. Original test sources unchanged. Earlier monolithic attempts exited 137 / JavaScript heap OOM; split full coverage succeeded.

validation.detailedReporterNote: The final-source 18-case gate was rerun after the origin.clone ownership restoration. The new source-special-final a/b logs and summary explicitly bind all 18 named cases to the final source SHA. Earlier source18 logs are retained as historical evidence rather than relied on for final-version assurance.
validation.countingNote: 18 new + 16 device + 3 projectile + 12 multistorey + 85 all-specials/imported Kraken = 134 distinct named cases. The earlier selected 7 all-specials cases are included in the final 85 and are not counted twice.

fullRegressionExecution.commands: All 17 exact command argument arrays are preserved in fullRegressionManifest.

earlierSpecialCommandsHistorical: node --max-old-space-size=512 --experimental-vm-modules --test --test-isolation=none --test-name-pattern='actual placement|booyah wall|target contacts|decoy prediction|production Level|booyah lifetime|enemy Ink Vac' patches/splatoon3/tests/special-trajectory.test.mjs

limitations: No Nintendo Switch capture comparison was performed.

Extracted tables omit inherited defaults; world scale, orbit speed, collision masks, some launch speed/offset, countershot wait semantics, and actor movement timelines retain documented runtime calibration.
Moving targets, manual cancellation and action-dependent body landing are represented as incomplete rather than fabricated fixed explosion points.
